Idempotency of Transfinite Cardinal Numbers Dr. BS Satpute Head, Department of Mathematics, Vaidyanath College, Parali, Beed, Maharashtra, India DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19115493 Corresponding Author: Dr. BS Satpute Abstract For transfinite cardinal number α, using Zorn’s lemma we have given a simple proof which is understandable to undergraduate students, of the result α + α = αα = α, that is, Idempotency for addition and multiplication. Keywords: Idempotency, Zorn’s lemma, Transfinite Cardinal Numbers, addition, multiplication

Introduction Let A and B be any two nonempty sets. A relation ρ from A to B is defined as a subset of A x B. Thus ρ is a relation from A to B if and only if (abbreviated by iff) ρ ⊆ A x B. In particular subset ρ of A x A is called a relation (or a binary relation) on A. We denote xρy for (x, y) ∈ ρ.

Theorem Let ~ be an equivalence relation in a nonempty set X and a and b be arbitrary elements in X. Then • a ∈ [a](ii) b ∈ [a] iff [a] = [b] iff a ~b. • Any two equivalence classes are either disjoint or identical.

A binary relation ρ on a set A is said to be • Reflexive if (a, a) ∈ ρ  a ∈ A. • Symmetric if (a, b) ∈ ρ ⇒ (b, a) ∈ ρ. • Anti-symmetric if (a, b) ∈ ρ and (b, a) ∈ ρ ⇒ a = b. • Transitive if (a, b) ∈ ρ and (b, c) ∈ ρ ⇒ (a, c) ∈ ρ.

Theorem Fundamental Theorem on Equivalence Relation: An equivalence relation ~ on a set X partitions the set X and conversely every partition of X induces an equivalence relation on X.

A relation ρ on a set A is called an equivalence relation on A if it is simultaneously reflexive, symmetric and transitive on A. An equivalence relation on a set is usually denoted by ~ (wiggle or tilde). Let ~ be an equivalence relation of a set X and let a ∈ X. The equivalence class of a, denoted by [a] or is defined as [a] = {x ∈ X | x ~a} = the set of those elements of X which related to a under ~. Let X be a nonempty set. A collection of nonempty mutually disjoint subsets of X whose union is X is called a partition of the set X.

Alternative statement: The distinct equivalence classes of an equivalence relation on X provides us with a decomposition of X as a union of mutually disjoint subsets. Conversely, given a decomposition of X as a union of mutually disjoint, nonempty subsets, we can define an equivalence relation on X for which these subsets are the distinct equivalence classes. A binary relation ρ on a set X is called a partial order relation if it is reflexive, anti-symmetric and transitive. Generally partial order relation is denoted by ≤ and a set with partial order elation is termed a partial ordered set (poset).
